title: password-policy — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins protocol::validate_min_length — the master-password minimum-length floor (MIN_PASSWORD_LEN = 12) enforced backend-side before any Argon2id work. Counts Unicode scalar values (str::chars().count()), NOT UTF-8 byte length. This is a boolean accept/reject CONFORMANCE category (not a byte-output category): an independent client that counts bytes instead of USVs diverges exactly on the multibyte cases. The frontend PasswordForm mirrors MIN_PASSWORD_LEN via a TS hand-constant; this category is the canonical cross-impl drift-check. Contract: design notes.md 2026-05-06 'Auth-pipeline backend MIN_PASSWORD_LEN floor; project-wide retroactive'.

vector_id.description: Stable identifier of the form 'password-policy/v0.1/<descriptive-slug>'. Immutable once shipped.

expected_kind.description: 'accept' ⇒ validate_min_length returns Ok(()); 'reject_too_short' ⇒ Err(ProtocolError::PasswordTooShort). Sub-floor length is the ONLY rejection cause at this layer — entropy gating is deliberately frontend-only (zxcvbn) and out of scope here.

input_password_utf8_hex.description: Candidate master password as UTF-8 bytes (hex, lowercase). Hex-encoded rather than a raw JSON string so leading/trailing whitespace, control chars, and multibyte scalars transport unambiguously. The empty string is allowed (decodes to zero bytes → reject_too_short).

informational_usv_count.description: Number of Unicode scalar values (str::chars().count()) in the decoded password — the value compared against MIN_PASSWORD_LEN (12). Informational: a port computes this itself, but it is pinned here so the USV-vs-byte distinction is auditable without running the reference impl.

informational_byte_len.description: UTF-8 byte length of the decoded password. On the multibyte cases this differs from informational_usv_count — a port that (wrongly) gates on byte length will mis-handle exactly those cases.
